NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — To prevent acid aerosol mist in zinc electrowinning, standard practice relies solely on tankhouse ventilation and cell-cover procedures. This intervention introduces a foam-blanket chemistry that increases gas-liquid interfacial resistance, suppressing aerosol entrainment by bubbles without altering cell or anode design. The closest existing practice is froth flotation in mineral processing, but this differs by using a non-ionic surfactant to stabilize a foam layer at the electrolyte surface, specifically targeting bubble burst aerosol mitigation. The mechanism acts by forming a cohesive foam barrier that dampens bubble rupture dynamics.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is aerosol mass flux ∝ bubble surface area × aerosol fraction per bubble. The foam blanket increases gas-liquid interfacial resistance by 50–100% (per supplier data for similar surfactants in acidic systems), reducing aerosol fraction per bubble by 30–60%. This directly reduces the aerosol mass flux. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = aerosol fraction per bubble; the mechanism moves it DOWN by increasing interfacial resistance via foam stabilization; this REDUCES aerosol entrainment.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
1. (b) Commercial non-ionic surfactant (e.g., polyethylene glycol alkyl ether, HLB 14–16), 10 ppm dosing rate, added to electrolyte recirculation line.  
2. (c) Adjust foam-blanket dosing pump schedule to operate during low-production hours (e.g., 22:00–06:00) to minimize operational impact.  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Standard practice: Ventilation system operation (continuous, energy cost) + cell-cover procedures (labor cost).  
- This intervention: Adds surfactant consumable (cost: ~$0.05/ton Zn, negligible vs. ventilation energy) + dosing pump schedule change (zero operational loss, as scheduled off-peak).  
- Burden class: Same (operational cost within 5%, no new hardware).  

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install foam-blanket system; monitor aerosol concentration at tankhouse breathing zone (using existing OSHA-style sampler) for 30 days. Pass/fail: Average aerosol concentration ≤50% of baseline (pre-intervention) for ≥80% of sampling points. Kill criterion: If concentration exceeds 80% of baseline at any point, halt and review surfactant dosage.  

MECHANISM CLASS: interfacial-resistance modulation via foam stabilization.
